name: heartlock
what: A tiny package that gives any project a heart.lock: what it is, why it exists, and whom it is for, in one line each.
why: AI, tools and teams keep changing; the heart should not. The why stays frozen in the repo where every human and every AI can read it.
whom: Makers building with AI who do not want their projects to drift.

name: drop
what: Send a file with a 6-letter code.
why: Sharing a file should need no account and no waiting.
whom: Anyone with a file and a friend.

name: zcurv.com
what: Abhinav Jha's home on the internet: who he is, what he builds, and how to reach him.
why: One address that is his, not a platform's, where his work stays findable whatever else changes.
whom: Anyone who wants to know what he builds: employers, collaborators, and the curious.

name: content-engine
what: One engine that makes and publishes every channel's videos: Interval and Mavi, a long and its Shorts every day.
why: Two channels, one system, so a daily video never depends on a day's motivation.
whom: Abhinav, the only operator; and through the channels, viewers who come for film essays and psychology.

name: Linux
what: An open-source operating system kernel that runs on everything from phones to supercomputers.
why: Software should be free to study, change, and share, all the way down to the core.
whom: Anyone who needs a foundation they can trust, inspect, and own.

name: Git
what: A distributed version control system for tracking changes in files and coordinating work.
why: People should be able to work together on code without losing history or trusting a central machine.
whom: Anyone who makes things in files and needs to remember, compare, and collaborate.

name: curl
what: A command-line tool and library for transferring data with URLs.
why: Moving data across networks should be reliable, scriptable, and available everywhere.
whom: Developers and systems that need to speak to the internet from the command line or from code.

name: SQLite
what: A small, self-contained SQL database engine that lives in a single file.
why: Reliable structured data should not require a server, setup, or maintenance.
whom: Developers who need a database that just works, embedded wherever data lives.

name: React
what: A JavaScript library for building user interfaces from components.
why: Complex interfaces become manageable when the UI is a clear function of state.
whom: Developers building interactive interfaces on the web and beyond.

name: Vue
what: A progressive JavaScript framework for building web user interfaces.
why: Building for the web should feel approachable without giving up power.
whom: Developers who want a framework that can start simple and grow with the project.

name: Kubernetes
what: An open-source system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.
why: Running software at scale should be declarative, resilient, and not tied to one machine.
whom: Teams operating applications that need to run reliably across many machines.

name: Docker
what: A platform for packaging and running applications in containers.
why: Software should run the same way everywhere, from a laptop to production.
whom: Developers and operators who want to ship applications without environment surprises.

name: VS Code
what: A free, extensible code editor for building and debugging modern software.
why: A developer's editor should be fast, capable, and shaped by the community that uses it.
whom: Developers who want one editor that adapts to every language and workflow.

name: Blender
what: A free, open-source 3D creation suite for modeling, animation, rendering, and more.
why: Professional creative tools should be available to everyone, not locked behind a price tag.
whom: Artists, studios, and learners who want to create 3D work without permission.

name: Wikipedia (MediaWiki)
what: The wiki platform that powers Wikipedia and other collaborative knowledge projects.
why: Human knowledge should be free for everyone to read, share, and improve.
whom: Communities that want to collect and share knowledge in the open.

name: Firefox
what: A free, open-source web browser built by Mozilla.
why: The web should stay open, private, and not controlled by a single company.
whom: People who want to browse the web on their own terms.

name: PostgreSQL
what: An advanced open-source relational database system.
why: Data deserves a store that is correct, extensible, and built to last decades.
whom: Developers and organizations who need a dependable database they can trust with important data.

name: Redis
what: An in-memory data structure store used as a database, cache, and message broker.
why: Some data needs to be read and written faster than a disk can go.
whom: Developers building systems that need fast, simple access to shared state.

name: Node.js
what: A JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine for running code outside the browser.
why: JavaScript should be useful beyond the page, for servers, tools, and scripts.
whom: Developers who want to build networked software with JavaScript.

name: Python
what: A programming language designed for readability and broad usefulness.
why: Programming should be clear enough that humans can read it, not just machines.
whom: Anyone who wants to turn ideas into working programs, from beginners to experts.

name: Rust
what: A programming language for building fast, reliable software.
why: Systems software should be both performant and safe, without trading one for the other.
whom: Developers who need low-level control without low-level memory bugs.

name: Go
what: A programming language built for simple, reliable, and efficient software.
why: Building and maintaining large software systems should stay straightforward.
whom: Teams building networked services and tools that need to be easy to read and operate.

name: WordPress
what: An open-source content management system for publishing on the web.
why: Publishing on the internet should be possible for anyone, not just developers.
whom: People and organizations who want to own and publish their own website.

name: ffmpeg
what: A complete, cross-platform toolkit for recording, converting, and streaming audio and video.
why: Working with media should not be blocked by formats, codecs, or proprietary tools.
whom: Anyone who needs to process audio or video, from hobbyists to production systems.

name: OBS Studio
what: Free, open-source software for video recording and live streaming.
why: Broadcasting yourself to the world should not require expensive or closed tools.
whom: Creators, educators, and anyone who wants to record or stream video.

name: Signal
what: A private messaging app with end-to-end encryption.
why: Private conversation should be the default, not a premium feature.
whom: Anyone who wants to communicate without being overheard.
